transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Good to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because for a long time now, I just wake up already feeling low. It's like... there's this heavy, gray feeling on me before I even get to the clinic for work, and it pretty much just follows me through the whole day.
How long have you been feeling this low most days?
Well, it's been going on for about two years and two months now. It started right around the time the staffing changed at the clinic, and my schedule just started rotating all over the place.
If your work schedule were stable again, do you think you would still feel this low most days?

I don't really know. I mean, the schedule change definitely started all this, but... honestly, it's been so long now that I can't really imagine not feeling this way. I'd like to think a normal schedule would fix it, but I'm just not sure anymore.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches as long as two months when you did not feel low most days?

No, not really. I mean, there might be a day or two here and there where I feel a little bit better, but... no, definitely not a whole two months. It's just been a constant thing for the whole two years.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I guess I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I still do the same stuff I usually do when I'm not at the clinic. It's just... I just feel down while I'm doing it. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest.
Do you often feel tired or low on energy?

Yeah, I do. I'm pretty much always tired. Even if I have a day off or manage to sleep in late, my body just... it still feels completely worn out. By the time I finish up at the clinic, you know, rooming patients and catching up on all the charts, it feels like I have absolutely nothing left in the tank. I don't have the energy to do my laundry, or go shoot hoops, or even just sit and mess with my electronics stuff. I'm just drained.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?
No, not really. My appetite is pretty much the same as it's always been. I still eat my regular meals and everything, so... yeah, no real change there.
Do you often feel bad about yourself or like you’re not good enough?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't really sit around feeling bad about myself or anything like that. I know I'm good at my job at the clinic, and I do the best I can. It's just the tiredness and feeling down that gets to me, not really feeling like I'm not good enough.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I have. It's really noticeable at work. I'll be staring at a patient's intake screen, and I just... I have to reread the same line over and over again for it to register. And I've caught myself missing little details, which isn't great. Like, I might miss medication doses on the chart, or I'll just completely mix up what I was about to ask the patient next. It's just hard to stay focused.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried a lot?
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel particularly anxious or worried about things. It's more just... feeling drained and down all the time. But no, I wouldn't say I'm dealing with a lot of anxiety.
During these past two years, has there ever been a period when your depression got much worse than your usual baseline for at least two weeks?

No, I don't think so. It's just been... kind of the same this whole time. Just this constant low, feeling tired and down. I haven't really noticed a time where it suddenly got a lot worse for a couple of weeks or anything. It's just always there, pretty much at the same level.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yeah, I do. I just keep thinking that this is how life is going to be now. Just... working random hours, always falling behind. It feels like I'm never going to get enough money, or even just the energy, to actually move forward with school or do anything better. So yeah, it feels pretty hopeless.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric for several days?

No, not at all. I can't really remember a time where I felt super energetic or... really happy like that for a few days. Honestly, I'm just exhausted most of the time, so nothing like that has happened.
If your work schedule became stable and stayed that way, do you think the low mood would continue?

I don't really know for sure. I mean... a stable schedule would be nice, and it might help with the physical exhaustion, but... I don't think it would actually fix my mood. Even on my days off when I don't have to worry about work, I still feel just as down. It feels like it's just kind of stuck with me now, no matter what my hours are. So, yeah, I think it would probably continue.
